entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioner is the 1st accused in Crime No.467/2024 registered by the Palai Police Station,
Kottayam, alleging the commission of the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 r/w Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. The petitioner has invoked the inherent jurisdiction of this Court under Section 528 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023, to quash all further proceedings in the above case.

It is asserted that the dispute that led to the registration of the crime has been amicably settled between the petitioner and the 2nd respondent, who has executed Annexure 2 affidavit, affirming the settlement.
I have heard the learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, the learned Public Prosecutor, and the learned Counsel for the 2nd respondent.
4. The learned counsel on either side submits that, with the intervention of relatives and well-wishers, the parties have resolved their disputes amicably.
The 2nd respondent has no subsisting grievance and does not wish to pursue the prosecution, and has no objection to the proceedings being quashed.
5. The learned Public Prosecutor, on instructions, submits that the Investigating Officer has reported that the parties have arrived at a genuine and bona fide settlement.
The State has no objection to the Criminal Miscellaneous case being allowed.

6. The scope and ambit of the inherent powers of this Court to quash criminal proceedings on the ground of settlement between the parties have been authoritatively CRL.MC NO. 10569 OF 2025 4 2025:KER:93941 laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court, in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303], State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan and Others [(2019) 5 SCC 688], Naushey Ali v. State of U.P. [(2025) 4 SCC 78], and in a host of judicial pronouncements.

entities.text: Gian Singh v. State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan and Others [(2019) 5 SCC 688]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Naushey Ali v. State of U.P. [(2025) 4 SCC 78]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is held that in cases where the offences are not grave or heinous, and where the parties have amicably settled the dispute, to secure the ends of justice, the High Court may invoke its inherent powers to quash the proceedings, particularly if continuation of the prosecution would serve no fruitful purpose.
Shankar P vs State Of Kerala on 4 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89764861/
2 7. On an overall consideration of the facts and circumstances of the present case, and the materials on record, I am satisfied that: the offences alleged are not heinous or of a serious nature; no public interest or element of societal concern is involved; the chances of conviction are remote in view of the settlement; and the continuation of the proceedings would merely burden the CRL.MC NO.
10569 OF 2025 5 2025:KER:93941 judicial process without advancing the cause of justice.

entities.text: Shankar P vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Furthermore, the settlement would promote harmony between the parties and restore peace.

Hence,
this Court is persuaded to hold that this is a fit case to exercise its inherent jurisdiction.
In the result, the Crl. M.C. is allowed.
Accordingly, Annexure 1 FIR and all further proceedings in Crime No. 467/2024 of the Palai Police Station, Kottayam, as against the petitioner, are hereby quashed.
